run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T10:42:16Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert signal is real but small and chronic. In Prometheus, frontend-proxy error spans exist only on span_name "ingress" with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR, running at 0.0037-0.0185 per second across the whole retained window while non-error ingress spans ran around 12.4-13 per second; the alert's current value 0.01111111111111111 equals the 10:42:16Z reading of that series. The one-hour increase of frontend-proxy error spans is 15.2, and in the 40 minutes to 10:59:45Z only frontend-proxy ingress (14.1) plus flagd EventStream spans in ad, recommendation and fraud-detection had any errors, while frontend, accounting, checkout and payment had none. The cause of the proxy errors is visible in its Envoy access log: HTTP 503 with response flag UC and code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on upstream cluster "frontend" for GET /, /api/products/* and /api/data/. In the sampled traces the same requests show a frontend-proxy ingress span with error=true/http.status_code=503 and a child "router frontend egress" span with error="true"/http.status_code="0", and those traces contain no frontend spans at all - the frontend never started answering. The load-generator's own GET spans record the 503. The error rate was already nonzero before the alert started (0.0048 at 10:18-10:23Z; 503 lines at 10:35:37Z and 10:36:25Z) and continued after it, so nothing stepped upward at 10:42:16Z. The pairing pod is healthy by its own state and signals: frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, startTime 10:03:18Z and no last termination, its deployment is 1/1 available, it produced no error spans and no memory-limit failures; it is CPU-saturated (0.103-0.111 cores against a 100m limit, 28.8-36.9% of CFS periods throttled). The only fault-injection found, chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition, applies PodNetworkChaos to fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, not to the frontend hop, so it does not match the observed failure path. Two separate things changed in the same minutes and are reported apart from this alert: fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst was OOMKilled (exit 137, restartCount 1) at 10:42:18Z, and the fraud-detection/kafka network-partition schedule keeps cycling each minute. The failure is therefore localized to the frontend-proxy -> frontend connection hop and best explained by the frontend closing upstream connections that Envoy reuses, but no single faulting object or setting is proven, so the root cause is left null and the remaining candidates are stated as hypotheses.

claims.text: The alerting signal is frontend-proxy ingress spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR: 5-minute rate 0.0037-0.0185 per second across 10:18-10:59Z against 12.4-13 per second of STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans; the series value at 10:42:16Z is exactly 0.011111111111111112, the number in the alert annotation.

The error volume is small: the one-hour increase of frontend-proxy error spans is 15.21, and in the 40 minutes ending 10:59:45Z the only series with error spans are frontend-proxy span_name "ingress" (14.13), fraud-detection "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (5.05), recommendation "/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (3.03) and ad "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (3.05); service_name frontend, accounting, checkout and payment are absent from that error set.

The frontend-proxy access log records the failures as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against upstream cluster "frontend" for GET / (767ms), GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO (800ms), GET /api/products/1YMWWN1N4O (389ms), GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N (1175ms), GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 (144ms) and GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars (155ms) between 10:35:37Z and 10:43:33Z.

In the sampled traces the failing requests show a frontend-proxy "ingress" span with error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR and a child "router frontend egress" span with error="true" and http.status_code="0"; those traces contain no frontend spans, and the load-generator's own GET spans carry error=true/http.status_code=503.

The error signal was already present before the alert start and persisted afterwards: frontend-proxy error-span rate was 0.0048/0.0043/0.0039/0.0037 per second at 10:18-10:27Z and 0.0037-0.0044 at 10:57-10:59Z, and 503 UC log lines are timestamped 10:35:37Z, 10:36:25Z, 10:40:53Z, 10:41:04Z, 10:41:37Z, 10:42:05Z and 10:43:33Z.

The failures are per-connection rather than a frontend outage: in trace 57250c0c8c15f32c8f07fb3d10fd5833 the proxy logged an ingress span with http.status_code=503 lasting 51504us starting 1794911529749346, and 54ms later an ingress span with http.status_code=200 lasting 1098921us that reached frontend POST /api/cart (200) and cart gRPC calls successfully.

The frontend upstream pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-17T10:03:18Z and an empty lastState (no terminated container), and deployment frontend reports replicas 1, ready 1, available 1 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend.

The frontend container is continuously pinned at its CPU limit: rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total) is 0.103-0.111 cores against a 100m limit for the whole window, with 0.288-0.369 of container_cpu_cfs_periods_total throttled; frontend-proxy uses 0.028 cores against its 30m limit with 0.043-0.083 throttled.

The frontend container shows no cgroup memory-limit failures: container_memory_failcnt is 0 for frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t (and frontend-proxy) at every step from 10:23:16Z to 10:59:16Z, although container_memory_working_set_bytes reads 246.3-257.8 MB against the deployment's 200Mi limit.

Latency at the proxy did not step at the alert time: histogram_quantile(0.99) of frontend-proxy "ingress" span duration reads 1232-1432 ms across the window, and the frontend service p99 reads 722-918 ms, both fluctuating without a change at 10:42:16Z.

The only chaos experiment observable in events is Schedule otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh), which spawns an experiment every minute (10:40:15Z-10:52:15Z shown) and whose Applied/Recovered messages name only otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst, one of the chaos targets, lost its container to OOMKilled: lastState.terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T10:42:18Z, restartCount 1, and Pod events Created/Pulled/Started for fraud-detection at 10:42:18Z; the deployment sets memory limit 400Mi.

All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, so no node-level resource failure is visible; frontend and frontend-proxy share node i-029c97e90b3730286, whose co-located accounting, cart, checkout, currency and product-catalog services show no error spans.

Endpoints resolve normally: service frontend has the single ready address 100.96.4.88:8080 and frontend-proxy 100.96.4.190:8080, and the proxy's access log shows the frontend upstream as 100.70.32.128:8080 (cluster service address) with cluster name "frontend".

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap has every demo fault flag at defaultVariant "off" (including adFailure, cartFailure, imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure), i.e. no enabled feature-flag fault at query time.

The chaos-mesh network partition (Schedule otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition) is not the cause of the frontend-proxy 503s: its Applied messages name only fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, whereas the observed failure is the frontend-proxy -> frontend upstream hop (flag UC on cluster "frontend"), and the 503s also occur outside its 55-second windows, e.g. 10:35:37Z, 10:36:25Z and 10:43:33Z.

A frontend pod crash, restart, rollout or OOM is not the cause: frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t has restartCount 0, empty lastState, Ready=True and startTime 10:03:18Z; its deployment is 1/1 available with no new ReplicaSet during the window; and service_name frontend has zero error spans.

Most likely mechanism for the UC resets: frontend-proxy (Envoy) reuses an idle upstream HTTP/1.1 connection to the single frontend pod that the frontend server has already closed, so the request is reset before response start; consistent with per-connection failures while other requests to the same pod succeed milliseconds apart, the 9ms-1175ms spread of the failed requests, and the absence of any frontend span for them.

The frontend container's sustained CPU saturation (0.103-0.111 cores against a 100m limit with 28.8-36.9% throttled CFS periods, and container_cpu_usage at the limit) may delay connection handling and contribute to these terminations; it is constant across the window, so it explains a chronic background error rate rather than the alert timing.

Because the annotation threshold is "above 0", the alert is plausibly firing on a chronic low-rate background of 503 UC errors (about 7 failed proxy requests per 40 minutes, ~0.03% of frontend-proxy spans in a 10-minute sample) rather than on a new degradation; the rule's own expression, threshold and for-duration could not be read, so this stays a hypothesis.

Align the proxy's upstream keep-alive/idle settings with the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive timeout (or enable health-checked/connection-refresh behaviour on the "frontend" cluster) so Envoy stops reusing connections the frontend has closed, and re-measure the 503 UC rate.

Raise the frontend CPU limit above its sustained ~0.10 core use and the frontend-proxy limit above its ~0.028 core use to remove the constant throttling as a confounding factor before concluding the alert is benign.

Confirm the RequestErrorRate rule's expression and consider a ratio-based or sustained-duration condition instead of "above 0", since the measured rate is chronically nonzero, and treat the fraud-detection OOMKill (memory limit 400Mi) and the recurring fraud-detection/kafka network-partition schedule as separate items to review.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules for that name returned no rules), so its expression, threshold and for-duration are unknown beyond the annotation text "above 0".
Metric series for this environment start at 10:18:16Z, about 24 minutes before the alert start, so no comparable baseline exists for whether the 503 UC rate is higher than in earlier hours or days.

The frontend container wrote no stdout/stderr lines at all in the checked window (fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines for frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t, and no previous instance exists), so the frontend-side reason for terminating the connections could not be read.

Envoy's upstream cluster configuration (keep-alive, idle timeout, max requests per connection, retry policy) is baked into the ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy image; the otel-demo namespace holds only flagd-config, otel-collector, product-catalog-products and kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMaps, so those settings could not be verified.
The chaos-mesh NetworkChaos and Schedule custom resources themselves (selector, action, direction, duration) are not readable with the available Kubernetes kinds; only their events were available.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series for the window (get_all_labels no_data), so there is no independent app-level HTTP 5xx ratio to quantify the impact.
The networkpolicies query returned nothing at all, which shows only that this query matched no object; the state of network policy at incident time is unknown.
No change_history integration is available, so configuration or rollout changes before the window cannot be compared.

The fraud-detection OOMKill's underlying memory growth driver was not investigated (only the OOMKilled reason, exit code 137 and 400Mi limit are established), and it is not tied to the frontend-proxy error signal.
Traces are a biased sample of the backend; the absence of frontend spans in the failing traces is evidence for those traces only and does not prove how many requests never reached the frontend.
next_steps: Read the alert rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source to confirm the expression, threshold and for-duration behind "RequestErrorRate".

Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap (cluster "frontend" upstream_http_protocol_options idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retries) and the frontend server's keep-alive settings, then test with an idle-timeout alignment.
Review the fraud-detection OOMKill (400Mi limit, exit 137 at 10:42:18Z) and decide whether its memory limit needs raising, separately from this alert.
Confirm with the environment owner whether the recurring chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition is an intended experiment.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.
